newsitem.title: UK: S&P RAISES LEGAL & GENERAL'S SENIOR DEBT RATINGS.
newsitem.headline: S&P RAISES LEGAL & GENERAL'S SENIOR DEBT RATINGS.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it raised its senior debt ratings of Legal& General Group Plc to AA from AA minus.
The move also covers Legal&General Finance Europe BV and Legal&General Finance Plc, which are guaranteed by the group.
"The outlook remains stable," S&P said in a statement. "The A1 plus commercial paper ratings of L&G and of Legal & General Finance plc are affirmed."
Separately, the rating agency said it affirmed Legal& General Assurance's long-term fund rating at AAA, based on excellent capitalisation and an increasingly strong business position.

S&P said it based its upgrade to the senior debt rating on a significant improvement in interest coverage and reduction in financial leverage, an improved business position, and strong operating performance in the past 18 months.

"Additionally L&G's capitalization, which was already excellent, has been bolstered further by the reclassification of 1.4 billion stg of reserves as shareholders' capital, which Standard & Poor's understands is to remain within the Long term Fund," the statement said.

L&G is a major life and pensions provider in the U.K., benefiting from a household name and sizable and diverse distribution capabilities, S&P said. In 1996 the company has leveraged on these strengths, growing its share of the U.K. life and pensions market strongly.

S&P said the group has a leading position in the household insurance sector, arising from its strong historic links with building societies and other mortgage lenders. In particular, its joint venture with Woolwich Building Society boosts L&G's share of this sector to over 5 percent of the company market.
"Long-term business will increasingly dominate the Group's total profits, thus reducing the future volatility of results," the statement said. codes: Wednesday, 18 June 1997 12:03:39 ENDS nFLLFJI80L
